activities.anchor: follows from a provable failure mode
activities.caption: walk the V-model, left arm down, right arm up
activities.name: seVOrder

config.prompt: The V-model's journey — put the stages in order:
items: Requirements decompose down the left arm into subsystem and component design
Units are verified as they are built
The whole is validated against the original need
config.why: Every requirement is born paired with the test that will check it — that pairing is what makes the right arm's climb possible at all.

activities.anchor: The canonical cases are systems cases
activities.caption: pair each case with its permanent lesson
activities.name: seCaseMatch

config.prompt: Two cases, one code — pair each with its lesson:

pairs.right: engineers said no below 53 °F on O-ring data; management overrode — the duty when authority and evidence diverge
the quartering-wind flaw disclosed; emergency welding saved the tower and nobody was hurt
safety, health and welfare of the public above employer, client and career
stakeholders, code clauses, options and consequences, escalate in good faith

config.why: The mechanism that makes the codes more than aspiration is case law and licensure — boards can revoke, and courts have cited the codes.

activities.anchor: The US model runs on four gates
activities.caption: stack the four gates in order
activities.name: seGatesOrder

config.prompt: From student to seal-and-sign authority — put the gates in order:
items: The PE exam — and the licence to seal and sign
config.why: The PE who stamps the drawing owns its consequences — and the board is the feedback element in a control loop on the profession, with continuing education as the corrective action.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — the megaproject overrun rate
activities.name: seOverrunEstimate

config.prompt: Bent Flyvbjerg's database of hundreds of major transport projects — roughly what share overrun their budgets?
config.why: Roughly nine in ten — average overruns about 20% for roads, 34% for bridges and tunnels, 45% for rail.
config.context: The fix is reference-class forecasting: predict from the distribution of similar past projects, not the current plan's enthusiasm.

activities.caption: true or false — the life-cycle ledger
activities.name: seLcaJudge

statements.s: Impacts migrate between life-cycle stages when you optimise only one.
statements.why: That is why LCA accounts cradle-to-grave: extraction, manufacture, transport, use, end of life.

statements.s: Recycled aluminium needs only about 5% of primary aluminium's energy.
statements.why: Which is why the recycling loop is worth more than the material swap.

statements.s: ISO 14040/44 standardises LCA's four steps so different studies can be compared.
statements.why: Goal and scope, inventory, impact assessment, interpretation — the requirements discipline applied to tonnes of CO₂-equivalent.

statements.s: Sustainability in engineering means energy efficiency.
statements.why: Energy is one line of a multi-line ledger: water, materials, toxicity, land use, end-of-life recoverability and social impacts all enter.

statements.s: Environmental impact statements became mandatory when NEPA required agencies to evaluate alternatives before committing (1970).
statements.why: The regulatory instruments grew from the same systems logic.

activities.anchor: Infrastructure designs are social contracts written in steel
activities.caption: walk the cost-driven switch like a systems engineer
activities.name: seFlintBranch

config.root: A city wants cheaper water. Walk the decision the way this lesson would.

start.text: Switch the water source to save money — which requirement must be written first?

choices.label: Corrosion control — the new source's chemistry against old pipes
choices.feedback: Flint's cost-driven switch went ahead without it, and leached lead city-wide.

choices.label: None — the new source meets the same standard
choices.feedback: Standards met line-by-line while the system-level requirement — no lead at the tap — went unwritten.

audit.text: The switch is approved in a meeting, each decision singly defensible. What makes the whole auditable?

choices.label: Trace who is exposed, by how much, verified how — and who is accountable when verification fails
choices.feedback: The systems translation: safety and equity are requirements to be traced, verified and audited like any other.

choices.label: A memo noting the change
choices.feedback: Documentation without traceability is the residue of nothing — the verification never existed.

end.text: Flint (2014–15): engineering decisions, singly defensible in a meeting, were systemically indefensible — and the professionals were charged.

config.why: A century of dam failures, from the Johnstown flood (1889, over 2,000 dead) to modern cases, traces to requirements that were never written down.

activities.anchor: The payoff is the same formalisation software engineering won from CI
activities.caption: which curve is the cost-of-change rule of thumb?
activities.name: seCostTrace

config.prompt: The aerospace rule-of-thumb cost-of-change curve — which curve is it?
config.why: A fix at integration is tens to hundreds of times costlier than the same fix at requirements — which is why MBSE's model-time checking pays for itself.

activities.anchor: Autonomous systems stress-test the code's assumptions
activities.caption: one line of the ethics reasoning is wrong — find it
activities.name: seFrontierSpot

config.prompt: An engineer drafts the safety case for an autonomous system. One line is wrong — click it:
lines: A threshold in the system's decision logic embeds a value judgement
The auditor's question: who decided the threshold, on what evidence, reviewed by whom?
Value judgements embedded in systems must be traceable — the requirements discipline extended to morality
The trolley problem is the core of self-driving ethics — solve it and the safety case is done
New clauses are being drafted: algorithmic accountability, data governance, dual-use responsibility
config.correction: The trolley-problem framing is mostly a distraction — the real questions are validation standards, liability allocation and transparency.
config.why: Traceable value judgements are the only version of machine ethics an auditor can actually use.
